content.user_title: Convert Pencil Designs to Frontend Code
content.value_statement: Pencil designs often lose detail when developers translate them by eye. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through precise extraction, implementation, and visual checks.
actual_capabilities: Inspects Pencil artboards, handoff nodes, variables, and screenshots before implementation.
Maps Pencil layout details into reusable frontend components and CSS tokens.
Preserves responsive artboard rules, fixed columns, spacing, typography, and touch target dimensions.
Handles background images, overlays, decorative layers, and image fill behavior with explicit CSS choices.
Uses browser screenshots and computed styles to compare implementation against Pencil designs.
limitations: Requires access to the relevant Pencil files, node IDs, screenshots, or exported assets.
Does not replace product requirements, accessibility review, or application logic design.
Visual accuracy depends on available fonts, assets, browser rendering, and project build tooling.
Works best when the user provides target artboard sizes and handoff notes.

use_cases.title: Implement a Marketing Page
use_cases.description: Convert a Pencil landing page into responsive HTML, CSS, or framework components while keeping the artboard layout intact.

use_cases.title: Match a Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Use node IDs, variables, and screenshots to resolve spacing, typography, and image crop differences during review.

use_cases.title: Migrate Legacy Screens
use_cases.description: Rebuild existing Pencil-designed screens in a modern frontend stack with reusable components and documented visual deviations.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Artboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pencil-to-code to convert this Pencil artboard into responsive frontend code. Preserve layout, typography, images, and spacing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single screen.

prompt_templates.title: Implement With Node IDs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pencil-to-code with these Pencil node IDs. Inspect the artboard, variables, repeated components, and assets before coding.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has specific Pencil nodes ready for implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Visual Fidelity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pencil-to-code to compare the current implementation with the Pencil screenshot and identify CSS changes for closer visual matching.
prompt_templates.scenario: The first implementation exists but does not match the design.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Responsive Component System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pencil-to-code to extract shared tokens and repeated units from these Pencil artboards, then implement reusable responsive components.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced work across multiple artboards or design states.

output_examples.input: A user provides a Pencil artboard for a product hero page and asks for implementation.
output_examples.output: The assistant extracts dimensions, typography, assets, and responsive rules, then delivers frontend components with matching visual structure.

output_examples.input: A user says the desktop version is too wide compared with the Pencil design.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks artboard widths, fixed foreground rules, and rendered screenshots, then recommends targeted layout and CSS token changes.

output_examples.input: A user needs repeated Pencil cards converted into a maintainable component.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies shared card properties, creates reusable structure, and preserves per-card text, icon, spacing, and image details.

best_practices: Provide Pencil node IDs, target artboard sizes, and exported assets before asking for code.
Run visual checks at every design breakpoint, not only common browser widths.
Keep reusable design tokens in the project theme or CSS variables.
anti_patterns: Do not approximate logos, photos, or illustrations when exported assets are available.
Do not stretch fixed foreground layouts just because the viewport is wider.
Do not rely only on screenshots when Pencil variables and node details are available.

faq.question: What is Pencil to Code for?
faq.answer: It helps convert Pencil design files and node IDs into frontend code with close visual fidelity.

faq.question: Does it require Pencil MCP access?
faq.answer: It works best with Pencil MCP access, but screenshots, node IDs, and exported assets can still guide implementation.

faq.question: Can it handle responsive layouts?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow emphasizes artboard-specific responsive rules, fixed columns, foreground stacks, and breakpoint screenshots.

faq.question: Can it create application logic?
faq.answer: It focuses on visual implementation. Business logic, data flows, and backend behavior need separate requirements.

faq.question: How does it check visual accuracy?
faq.answer: It compares browser screenshots with Pencil screenshots and uses computed styles for typography and spacing issues.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
